facts.text: I have a tremor in my hand.
Only in the right hand.
I noticed it about 6 months ago.
Lately it seems to be getting worse.

facts.item: tremor: what you are doing when it shakes
facts.text: It shakes when I'm just sitting around doing nothing.
It usually stops when I hold out the remote control to change the channel.
Nothing makes it better.
It seems more severe when I'm really tired.
I don't think I have any other symptoms.
My wife says I've slowed down because I can't keep up with her when we go grocery shopping, but I think that's just because I retired last year.
I've noticed myself walking more slowly recently.
When I was in college, I occasionally had a hand tremor.

facts.item: earlier tremor: what brought it on
facts.text: It came after I pulled an all-nighter and drank lots of coffee.
It was in both hands, but it was worse in the right.

facts.item: earlier tremor: compared with the tremor now
facts.text: It seemed faster than the one I have now.
I have high cholesterol, which I manage through diet.
I have asthma.
I've never injured my head.
I don't have any medication allergies.
I use an albuterol inhaler for my asthma as needed.
I haven't used it in more than a year.
Both of my parents were alcoholics.
My parents died in a car accident in their 40s.
My sister is healthy.
I think my father may have had a tremor, but I'm not sure.
I have one cup of coffee each morning.
I used to have three cups a day, but I've cut down in recent months.
I don't drink. Since both of my parents were alcoholics, I avoid it.
I don't smoke.
I don't use any drugs.
I've become quite inactive lately.
I'm married.
I live with my wife.
I'm a former professor of chemistry.
I retired last year.

findings.result: Clear breath sounds on both sides.

findings.result: Regular rate and rhythm; normal S1 and S2; no murmurs, rubs or gallops.

findings.result: Alert and oriented to person, place and time.

findings.name: tremor examination
findings.result: Resting pill-rolling tremor of the right hand that improves or disappears with purposeful action or posture.

findings.name: muscle tone
aliases: passive movement of the wrists and arms
findings.result: Mild rigidity in both wrists and arms, which are stiff and move slowly on passive movement; no frank cogwheeling.

findings.name: reflexes
findings.result: Deep tendon reflexes symmetric and 2+ in all extremities.

findings.name: coordination
findings.result: Rapid alternating movements and heel-to-shin test normal and symmetric.

findings.name: gait
findings.result: Bradykinetic gait with small shuffling steps and a slightly bent-forward posture.

findings.name: sensation
findings.result: Intact to light touch and pinprick.

other_considerations.note: Midbrain injury from stroke, trauma or demyelination can rarely cause a solitary asymmetric resting tremor.
Many drugs enhance physiologic tremor, including beta-agonists such as albuterol; neuroleptics and metoclopramide cause parkinsonism, often without tremor.
Frequency varies and the tremor becomes irregular or stops during a complex repetitive task with the other limb.
Can cause resting tremor but is not typically considered after age 40.
Causes a fine tremor together with other classic signs and symptoms.

source_issues: Chief complaint is malformed in the raw sheet: the patient's complaint 'I have a tremor in this hand (points to right hand).' is printed inside the doctor's line, and the answer field 'Only in the right hand.' repeats the p001 answer. The opening fact uses the complaint; the stage direction is an acting note.

The note HPI says 'He has noticed walking more slowly recently'; in the script he denies other symptoms and attributes his wife's comment about slowing down to retirement (p006). Added as from-note fact f011 with a flag.
The note says the college tremor occurred 'when very fatigued'; the script says after all-nighters and drinking lots of coffee.
The note says 'reducing caffeine intake to 1 cup of coffee daily did not provide relief'; the script never asks this directly (only p004 'Does anything make it better? No.').
The note PMH says 'Mild asthma'; the patient does not grade his asthma.
Gold rank-3 (physiologic tremor) lists 'Resting tremor' as its history finding, which does not fit physiologic tremor and looks copied from rank 1.
Gold rank-1 exam finding 'Low-frequency tremor' has no frequency in the note exam; only the patient's comparison (the college tremor 'seemed faster', p007) supports it.
e008 says 'normal and symmetric Romberg', which is unusual wording for a Romberg test; recorded as normal.
notes: Coffee: current one cup each morning (f026) and the former three cups a day, cut down in recent months (f027, resolved).
Albuterol: as-needed prescription (f020, present) and no use in more than a year (f021, absent recent use), relevant to the gold's drug-induced tremor consideration.
p006 is split into the denial of other symptoms (f009), the wife's observation with his explanation (f010) and retirement last year (f035).
The father's possible tremor is kept as present with the patient's uncertainty in the text (f025).

SP-simulated rigidity, posture, gait and resting tremor (v1 x019-x022) agree with the note exam and are merged into the matching records: tremor (x010), muscle tone (x011) and gait with posture (x016). The SP notes do not name the hand; the script and the note say right.
Note exam wording 'soft touch' is rendered as light touch.

Conversion: the opening text says 'my hand' rather than 'this hand' because the patient model cannot point; the side is the location child f002 ('Only in the right hand.', complete list). f001 has no quote because the complaint sits in the cc question line, which the coverage check does not search.
Conversion: the college tremor (v1 f011-f013) is a parent 'earlier episodes of tremor' (f012) with context, location and comparison children.

Conversion: v1 f029 ('has become quite physically inactive lately', present) keeps its polarity under the neutral label 'change in physical activity' (f031); the text drops the leading 'No' so the wording matches the present polarity.
Conversion: p013 is split into marital status (f032) and living situation (f033); v1 had one fact.

Conversion: the note's 'Vital Signs: Within normal limits' (e002) agrees with the doorway values, so it is cited in each doorway vital record. The Romberg test has its own record (x015); rapid alternating movements and heel-to-shin form the coordination record (x014).
